summary.headline: Gujarat Energy Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59% YoY to ₹9,826 crore and PAT rose 22% to ₹639 crore, while Morbi industrial volumes normalised sharply.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 59% YoY to ₹9,826 crore, EBITDA rose 20% to ₹2,019 crore and PAT rose 22% to ₹639 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹19,496 crore (+61%), EBITDA ₹2,502 crore (+43%) and PAT ₹1,637 crore (+51%). Total CGD volumes grew 24% YoY to 10.7 mmcmd in Q2, but Morbi ceramic demand fell from about 8 mmcmd in Q1 to about 3.8 mmcmd in Q2 (about 1 mmcmd currently). Management signalled a new growth phase (CBG entry, six LNG stations, long-term LNG contracts) with investment plans due with Q3 results.

segments.name: City gas distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Total CGD volume 10.7 mmcmd in Q2 (+24% YoY) and 11.5 mmcmd in H1 (+31% YoY). Industrial PNG 6.1 mmcmd in Q2 (+39% YoY); H1 industrial 6.9 mmcmd. CGD realisation ₹4.63/scm vs ₹4.65 in Q1 per Q&A.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Q2 CNG volume 3.67 mmcmd (+11% YoY); H1 3.72 mmcmd. Added 18 stations in H1 to 857 total; target 75+ stations in FY27. Domestic CNG base about 25.3 lakh connections.

segments.name: Gas trading (CGT)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹7,615 crore (+84% YoY), H1 ₹14,749 crore; EBITDA ₹329 crore (+89%). Management cited trading margin of about 4% in Q2 vs higher in Q1; H1 guidance around 7% per management, while separately guiding 5-6% for H2.

segments.name: Power subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Two power plants running at low utilisation due to energy shortage; losses under review with utilities to build a turnaround plan. Standalone PAT is about ₹149 crore lower than consolidated per analyst question.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance reiterated at about ₹1,000 crore, focused on CGD infrastructure.
Gas trading margin guided at 5-6% going forward, kept conservative given geopolitical uncertainty.
CGD margin per SCM guided at ₹5-6; Q2 actual about ₹4.7 per management.
Morbi guidance: current volumes about 1 mmcmd; management expects pricing to be competitive vs propane.
Investment plans for CBG, LNG and growth strategy to be announced with Q3 results.
Expected income tax refund of about ₹900 crore, anticipated by end of FY27 after merger-related filings.
Target of 75+ CNG stations in FY27 and double-digit CNG volume growth.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex ₹181 crore; H1 FY27 capex ₹308 crore; FY27 guidance about ₹1,000 crore.
LNG terminal (Mundra) utilisation about 24% in Q2; firm capacity booked at Mundra.
Board approved long-term Henry Hub-linked LNG sourcing of 0.8 MTPA for up to 10 years, priced about $7-9/MMBtu DES.
Exploring six LNG stations in GAs for long-haul transport; CBG EOI issued to partners.
Propane-related infrastructure still under evaluation; no decision yet.
Current LNG long-term book about 3 mmtpa (Qatar 1.0 + 0.3 + Unipar 0.4 + Shell 1.0 approx); target net book about 4 mmtpa.
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic volumes: Q1 about 8 mmcmd, Q2 about 3.8 mmcmd, current about 1 mmcmd.
Morbi price differential vs propane about ₹8/scm; about ₹10/scm in September.
Gas sourcing mix in Q2: ~55% imported, 29% other domestic and RLNG, 10% APM, 6% new well gas.
Gas trading sourced 12.31 mmcmd; 4.67 mmcmd sold externally and 7.63 mmcmd to CGD. Total company gas sales 15.38 mmcmd.
Management plans to diversify industrial demand beyond Morbi (Rajkot, Surendranagar, Surat, Morbi peers, Ankleshwar, Vapi and others).
LNG share in Q2 sourcing about 50%; HPHT volumes 1.3 mmcmd per management.

qa_highlights.question: Treasury: how much is parked with GSFS at 30 Sep, and is GSFS requiring the company to hold funds tied to the GSPC LNG loan?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposits with GSFS are about ₹3,300 crore. Management said there is no linkage with the GSPC LNG loan, which was refinanced by GSFS earlier for better rates; new surplus is placed with the bank offering the highest rate under a board-approved policy.

qa_highlights.question: Tax refund from merger: amount and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Returns are filed; refund of about ₹900 crore expected by financial year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Gas trading margin: why was Q2 lower than Q1 and is H2 guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margin was higher and Q2 about 4%, and maintained 5-6% guidance for H2 citing geopolitical uncertainty. It denied negative margin on fertiliser contracts linked to Brent.

qa_highlights.question: Morbi volume trajectory and propane competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi was about 3.8 mmcmd in Q2 and about 1 mmcmd currently; pricing will be set competitively against propane, which is about ₹8/scm cheaper currently (₹10 in September). Propane infrastructure still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Basis of $7-9 LNG pricing on the new 0.8 MTPA contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is Henry Hub-linked, on a DES basis, with the underlying Henry Hub assumption around $3.3-3.5/MMBtu per management. Seller bears freight and insurance.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone vs consolidated PAT gap and power subsidiary losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses at two power subsidiaries are under review; management is talking to utilities for a turnaround plan. The LNG subsidiary is at about 24-25% utilisation and now cash-profitable.

risks_watch: Morbi demand volatility: volumes fell from about 8 mmcmd to about 1 mmcmd; industrial growth depends on diversification beyond Morbi.
Trading margin guidance (5-6%) vs H1 actuals; Q2 margin around 4% per management.
Working capital swing: inventories up to ₹2,500 crore from ₹990 crore, trade payables up to ₹3,561 crore, receivables up to ₹2,420 crore (standalone).
Power subsidiaries continue to make losses; turnaround plan pending.
Gas sourcing cost and geopolitical volatility, with LNG price and freight exposure.
Q3 investment plan announcement for CBG, LNG and growth strategy; large cash balance (about ₹7,000 crore per analyst) with capex only about ₹1,000 crore in FY27.
Several analyst data requests were deferred (Q1/Q2 FY26 trading volume split, LNG contract-wise volumes).
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and integrated sourcing, but guarded on gas trading margins and Morbi outlook, citing geopolitical uncertainty. Several detailed figures were deferred to the investor presentation or follow-up, and the transcript quality limits precision on some numbers.
key_quotes: Our integrated model therefore remains central to our strategy helping us navigate near-term industry volatility while providing a strong foundation for sustainable and profitable growth.
We reiterate our FY 27 capex guidance of approximately 1000 crores with investments focused largely on strengthening our CGD infrastructure and supporting future volume growth.
There is no linkage between the two that we are parking funds with GSFS and they are giving in loans to the extent of GSPC LNG.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: CGD margin guidance cut to ₹5-6/scm (Q2 actual about ₹4.7) and gas trading margin guided 5-6% vs Q2 about 4%, with Q1 margin higher, so margins are guided down, not up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 75+ CNG stations targeted in FY27 (857 total after 18 added in H1) and six LNG stations being explored, but LNG terminal utilisation is only about 24% so large new firm capacity is not needed yet.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: CGD volume grew 24% YoY to 10.7 mmcmd and CNG is guided to double-digit growth, but Morbi fell from about 8 mmcmd in Q1 to about 1 mmcmd now, so net volume growth depends on diversifying away from Morbi.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said CBG, LNG and growth investment plans will be announced with Q3 results, though FY27 capex is held at about ₹1,000 crore (H1 ₹308 crore) against a large cash pile of about ₹7,000 crore per analyst.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut CGD margin guidance to ₹5-6/scm and kept gas trading margin at 5-6% citing geopolitical uncertainty, with Q2 trading margin about 4%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas trading margin Q2 about 4% against 5-6% H2 guide, and Morbi at about 1 mmcmd vs 8 mmcmd in Q1, with power subsidiaries still loss-making and no turnaround plan yet.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CBG entry and six LNG stations are at EOI or exploration stage with investment plans due with Q3 results, and propane-related infrastructure is still under evaluation with no decision.

rows.label: Power subsidiaries turnaround plan
rows.why: Two power plants run at low utilisation due to energy shortage and losses are under review with utilities, so a turnaround plan is pending but not yet agreed.

rows.label: Working capital unwind
rows.why: Standalone inventories rose to about ₹2,500 crore from ₹990 crore and payables to ₹3,561 crore, so the swing could reverse as gas prices and Morbi volumes settle.

rows.label: Income tax refund of about ₹900 crore
rows.why: Returns are filed after merger-related filings and management expects a refund of about ₹900 crore by financial year-end, which would boost cash.
